from math import gcd


def best_average(a: list[int], k: int) -> list[int]:
    n = len(a)
    prefix = [0] * (n + 1)
    for idx, x in enumerate(a):
        prefix[idx + 1] = prefix[idx] + x

    # Current candidate ratio p/q (q >= 1), starting from the whole array.
    p, q = prefix[n], n

    # Dinkelbach iteration: maximize sum - (p/q) * length over subarrays of
    # length >= k, scaled by q to stay in exact integer arithmetic. Stop when
    # no subarray gives a strictly positive value, meaning p/q is optimal.
    while True:
        best_val = 0
        best = None
        min_val = None
        min_i = -1
        for j in range(k, n + 1):
            i = j - k
            v = q * prefix[i] - p * i
            if min_val is None or v < min_val:
                min_val = v
                min_i = i
            cur = (q * prefix[j] - p * j) - min_val
            if cur > best_val:
                best_val = cur
                best = (min_i, j)
        if best is None:
            break
        i, j = best
        p, q = prefix[j] - prefix[i], j - i

    g = gcd(p, q)
    return [p // g, q // g]
